definitions.gloss: short time; brief period; short duration
definitions.explanation: A relatively brief span of time. Often used as a modifier with で or の to describe doing something quickly or in a limited time.

examples.japanese: {短時間|たんじかん}で{終|お}わらせる。
examples.english: I'll finish it in a short time.

examples.japanese: {短時間|たんじかん}の{勤務|きんむ}を{希望|きぼう}しています。
{短時間|たんじかん}でこれだけの{成果|せいか}を{出|だ}せたのは、チーム{全員|ぜんいん}の{努力|どりょく}のおかげだ。
examples.english: The fact that we could achieve this much in such a short time is thanks to the effort of the entire team.

notes:
USAGE:
A compound of {短|たん} (short) + {時間|じかん} (time). Used as a noun, often followed by で (in a short time) or の (short-time ~). Very common in work contexts for part-time or reduced-hours positions.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {短時間|たんじかん}で (in a short time)
- {短時間|たんじかん}{勤務|きんむ} (short-hour work)
- {短時間|たんじかん}{労働|ろうどう} (short-time work/employment)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {長時間|ちょうじかん}: long time — the antonym
- {短期間|たんきかん}: short period — measured in days, weeks, or months rather than hours
